newsitem.title: USA: Clinton vows to press for Hong Kong freedoms.
newsitem.headline: Clinton vows to press for Hong Kong freedoms.

text.p: President Bill Clinton assured a Hong Kong democracy advocate on Friday the United States is pressing China to honour the colony's democratic freedoms when it resumes sovereignty on July 1.

Briefing reporters on a meeting between Clinton and Hong Kong democracy leader Martin Lee, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said: "The president said China should not only uphold the economic freedoms that have been so important to the people of Hong Kong but should also continue to extend civil and political freedoms to the people of Hong Kong."

McCurry said continuation of Hong Kong's civil liberties were indispensable to nuturing the colony's booming economic environment. "The president strongly shared the view, expressed also by Mr. Lee, that support for the rule of law, that press freedoms, that freedom of speech, freedom of assembly and the liberties that have been associated with the people of Hong Kong should and must continue," he said.

"We've said often that the full benefit of our (U.S.-Chinese) bilateral relationship cannot ever be fully realised while there are impediments in the relationship," McCurry said in response to questions. "Clearly any diminution of the the freedoms enjoyed by the people of Hong Kong would be a serious impediment in our relationship."

He declined to say what Washington might do specifically if China carried through with announced restrictions on some political activities, but commented: "There would be consequences for any erosion of the freedoms and liberties that are currently enjoyed by the people of Hong Kong."

Clinton is treading a fine diplomatic line between a desire for strong ties with China and a desire to uphold traditional democratic values in the Hong Kong issue. His participation in Lee's visit was carefully orchestrated, and McCurry said he had joined a 45-minute meeting between Lee and Vice President Al Gore for about 25 minutes.
